_about: My validity review of roadmap 6b's accepted scenarios, before any run (the standing rule), by the PI's criteria of 2026-09-28: a near miss is flawed when the agent cannot check it through the API (or the service cannot have it), or when a natural reading of the request includes it. Ids are not reviewed: every test runs with opaque ids. Verdicts per scenario and per near miss (by the writer's ids).

G4-BOX-09.note: A file's tasks (action, is_completed, due_at) are readable through the API; due 2026-07-15T17:00Z is July 15 in every US zone; a to-do ('complete') task, a completed review, and tasks due July 16 or 28 are clearly not 'a still-open review task due July 15'.

G4-LIN-10.note: Priority, title and updatedAt are readable through the GraphQL API; the update times fall on the same calendar day in UTC and every US zone (Sep 13 10:00Z is Sep 13 in the US); PAY-5's due date on the 12th is a date-confusion trap, not a second reading.

decoys.8201: valid: the reader's flag (a year suffix could still be 'the Seaport Archive folder') is the usual near-name trap; the request gives the name exactly, unlike the PI's group B, where the request left the property open

G4-BOX-11.note: Name, description and tags are readable through the API; three folders named Seaport Archive in different parents are possible in Box; 'tagged harbor' is a tag, and the lighthouse must be in the description.

G4-CAL-09.note: Attendees' response status and all-day vs timed are readable; June 21, 2018 is the Thursday after Calendar's fixed day (Sunday June 17); 'Team offsite debrief' is not 'the team offsite'.

G4-LIN-09.note: A workflow state's name, type and team are readable through the API. A state named 'Completed' is not a Review state; 'Final Review' is a started state, not a completed one; Mobile Web is not the Mobile team.

decoys.i-delta-1: valid: owning the parent team Growth does not make Delta 'the team Priya Nair owns'; the issue's team is Delta

G4-LIN-11.note: Team memberships and their owner flag are readable. With Maya's onboarding checklist issue, the owner condition picks Atlas alone.

G4-BOX-12.note: A file's owner, creator and last modifier are in its details; Maya Lopez is not Maya Chen; a comment by Leo does not make him the last modifier.

decoys.8105: valid: Omar's comment is addressed to Priya ('Priya Nair - ... please countersign'), not written by her; the author is readable

G4-BOX-13.note: Comments (author, message) and tasks are readable per file; the phrase in a description, in a task, or in someone else's comment is not Priya's comment.

G4-BOX-14.note: A file's lock, version number and tags are in its details; a shared link is not a lock; 'renewal' in a description is not the tag.

G4-LIN-12.verdict: weak but valid: contrived, five users share the display name Rae Ellison

decoys.i-d2: valid: 'Rae Ellison-Quinn' is a near-name variant; the request gives the name exactly

G4-LIN-12.note: Display name, status label and time zone are readable per user; the scenario leans on five same-named users told apart by status and zone, as G4-SLK-01 leans on a user named by email.

G4-LIN-13.note: 'Current cycle' depends on today: Cycle 12 runs 2026-09-21 to 10-05 and is flagged active; written 2026-09-28, so its clock puts the agent inside Cycle 12, where the dates and the flag agree.

decoys.i-mob-1: valid, borderline (flag for the PI): an issue has one team, and Platform Mobile is not Platform; Linear shows sub-team issues in the parent team's views, so a reader may take it as in Platform, a weaker trap like G4-BOX-05's natural ambiguity
decoys.i-mob-2: valid, borderline (flag for the PI): as i-mob-1, and its parent issue is in Platform

G4-LIN-15.note: Team name, state and assignee are readable; the two sub-team near misses test H:Team.parentId and are ruled as G4-LIN-11's Delta near miss.

G4-LIN-16.verdict: weak but valid: contrived phrasing ('the active human admin')
G4-LIN-16.note: A user's active, admin and app flags are readable through the API; each near miss fails one of the three.

G4-LIN-17.note: Issue relations (type, direction, related issue) are readable; 'blocks X' excludes an issue X blocks, a merely related one, and one whose blocking and link sit on different relations.

G4-LIN-19.note: The replica's `projects` query errors, but projects are reachable through searchProjects and a document's project, and projectUpdate works (replica notes). The deciding facts are on documents (creator; one document holding both title and authorship); all three projects are at risk, so health decides nothing.

decoys.8112: valid: a file in a subfolder is not in the folder itself (the PI's reading of G4-BOX-06's hint)

G4-BOX-02.note: Favorites is Box's real collection, readable through /collections and a file's details; hubs and folders are distinct; the budget spreadsheet must be one file.

G4-BOX-15.note: Hub title, description and created date are readable (the development round's hub scenario was accepted); a created-January hub updated on March 4 is not 'created on March 4'.

decoys.ev_sprint_fakelink: flawed (group B): 'the sprint review with a video link' naturally includes an event whose description holds a Meet link; only its conference field is empty (as AP-SLK-04's message blocks)
decoys.ev_sprint_oak: valid, borderline (flag for the PI): Oak Room is the booked room resource and Maple Room is only location text; 'has Maple Room booked' reads as the booking
decoys.ev_sprint_plainmaple: valid: the room's attendee entry is not a resource, which the agent can read in the replica (the PI's AR-BOX-21 ruling)

G4-CAL-10.note: Status, conference link and room resources are readable per event.

G4-CAL-08.note: Visibility, event type and calendar are readable; two calendars named Engineering are told apart by Sprint Planning on Thursday afternoon, as the request does.

G4-LIN-14.note: Team, project and assignee are readable per issue; each near miss splits the conditions across issues or swaps creator for assignee.

G4-LIN-20.note: A comment's author, body, issue and parent are readable (the top-level comments query works); the sub-issue's comment is on a different issue.

G4-LIN-21.note: A milestone's status and target date are readable (the development round's milestone scenario was accepted); 'next' depends on today, which its clock (the day it was written) fixes.

G4-SLK-09.note: A user's title, time zone and active status are readable through users.info; 'in Chicago' is the Chicago time zone.
